Continue the Wilson-lines investigation in the shifted-zeta-positivity repo:
papers/susy-positivity/investigations/wilson-lines. Working manuscript 0.3 is
"Deformation flows for the shifted Weil family: the transfer as an all-pass
filter". Take your time on the mathematics; I would rather have one result
that survives than a survey.

Read first, in this order, and don't re-derive the framing from them:
  notes/CONTINUATION_20260917.md          - state, the eight facts, what not to redo
  notes/SAMPLING_AND_THE_DEFICIT_20260917.md - the current front
  manuscript.pdf sections 4 and 7        - the all-pass identification and the region

THE TASK. Settle, or sharply bound, the lower frame bound of the Riemann zeros
as a sampling set for the Paley-Wiener space PW_{L/2}. Under RH that bound *is*
lambda_min(Q_{0,L}), so "how does the margin collapse" is a question in sampling
theory with the generating function - xi itself - in hand. Four steps, in order:

(a) Literature. Suzuki arXiv:2301.00421 (the Hilbert space of the Weil
    distribution as a de Branges space; a totally ordered chain; inequalities
    converted to equalities) is now machinery, not background: the de Branges
    question and the frame-bound question coincide. Also the non-uniform
    sampling literature for PW spaces - Beurling, Landau, Seip,
    Ortega-Cerda-Seip, Lyubarskii-Seip. The specific question: for a zero set of
    superlinear density generated by a Hermite-Biehler function, what does the
    theory give for frame bounds on PW_a at types a below the critical one?
    If it gives an expression through the structure function, that is the
    theorem to chase.

(b) A basis adapted to the deficit. The obstruction lives below
    tau_c = 2 pi e^L, with maximal sample deficit D(L) = 2 e^L - 7/4 exactly.
    Recompute upper bounds on lambda_min with trial functions built from that
    band - prolates at bandwidth tau_c, not at gamma_1, and not polynomials.
    Calibrate against Zhu's certificates (2.3e-17 at L=0.8, 3.2e-283 at L=2,
    normalised against ||f||_2^2). Until this is done no decay law is testable.

(c) A control. Repeat (b) with an artificial zero set of the same density
    (1/2pi) log(tau/2pi) but no arithmetic. If the decay tracks D(L), the
    collapse is a density effect and not an arithmetic one, which would be a
    large structural statement in either direction. This is cheap; do it even if
    (b) is only partly done.

(d) If (a)-(c) yield something, ask what it says about the two-sided question:
    strict positivity is already proved by a counting argument (sampling note,
    section 3), so the content is entirely in the rate.

FALLBACK, if the above stalls: the group-delay test of manuscript Condition 9.1
on a protected open Wilson line two-point function in the defect setting of
arXiv:1102.4948 - extract the phase against the dilatation eigenvalue and
compare its derivative with 2 theta'(tau). No arithmetic, no positivity, and it
is the first test in this program a gauge theory can fail.

TRAPS, each of which has already cost time:
  - a_omega has poles at Re p = +omega, so its continuation to the imaginary
    axis is NOT the causal symbol; the residues crossed there are the entire
    form. K_omega may be contour-shifted to the axis; a_omega may not. Same for
    the Cayley symbol a_cum.
  - The apparent poles of a_omega at +-1/2 +- omega cancel between the three
    factors of xi. Do not attribute them to a_omega.
  - Dilation in x, i.e. r -> r^lambda, is not a conformal map. Dilation in r is,
    and the Weil form is exactly invariant under it. Do not repeat the argument
    that conformal invariance forbids the target; it is corrected in 0.3.
  - Every recorded margin in this program is a trial-space Rayleigh quotient,
    hence a basis-dependent upper bound. Two independent computations differ by
    ~250 orders of magnitude at L=2. Do not fit a law to them; say so if you are
    tempted.
  - Rayleigh quotients are one-sided. State, every time, which direction a value
    certifies.
  - Manuscript Proposition 8.2 (the rank-one endpoint variation) is a partial
    derivative at fixed omega. Along a path the motion is endpoint plus bulk.

STANDARDS. Classify every statement in the text as a written proof, a proof
sketch, a labelled numerical computation, a heuristic, or a reading, and label
anything conditional on RH. Check the algebra independently rather than
inheriting it. Prefer a sharp negative result to a vague positive one. If the
direction looks wrong to you, say so plainly - that is more useful to me than
progress on a bad line.

CONVENTIONS. Research notes in notes/, reviews in reviews/, with the Claude
model named at the top of anything you write. Check programmes are standard
library only, print JSON to stdout, keep a preserved record under
numerics/records/, and are registered in the CHECKS dictionary of
validation/drafts.py; anything needing mpmath goes in numerics/exploratory/ and
is labelled unregistered. Snapshot before replacing a manuscript version
(drafts.py save YYYY-MM-DD-vNN); everything under 1 MiB per the repo's
LARGE_FILES policy. If a git command leaves a stale .git/index.lock, tell me.

Write results to notes first. Only change the manuscript when I ask. End the
session with a continuation note in notes/.

**The thing you most need to know first: there is a units error in the programme, and it has been driving a wrong conclusion.** Zhu (arXiv:2608.24827) supports $f$ in $[-L,L]$; this investigation supports $f$ in $(-L/2,L/2)$. **Zhu's $L$ is half of yours.** Once matched, the sampling note's "250 orders of magnitude" discrepancy evaporates: I rebuilt $Q_{0,L}$ from scratch (sine basis, every element closed-form from the explicit formula) and reproduce the three recorded CriticalPath margins to 2.2%, 3.2% and 0.2%, and land inside Zhu's certified enclosure at the matching horizon. The recorded numbers are *not* weak basis-dependent bounds. Sampling-note §5 is withdrawn; manuscript Prop 7.6 and Remark 7.7 do **not** need the qualification it proposed. The assembler agrees with your own pre-existing quadrature assembler to $6\times10^{-25}$.

**The result.** The four steps gave three negatives and one structural fact.

- **(a)** Closed. Suzuki's de Branges structure function is $\xi(\tfrac12-iz)+\xi'(\tfrac12-iz)$, not $\Xi$, and the paper is purely structural; Ortega-Cerdà–Seip give a dichotomy, not a constant; Beurling's gap theorem applies only for $L<\pi/\gamma_1=0.2223$. There is no theorem to chase through the structure function.
- **(b)** The deficit band is the right *scale* — the obstruction's frequency profile is universal in $W/\tau_c$, stable to ±1% across $10^{80}$ in $\lambda_{\min}$ — but the literal construction (vanish at the sub-critical zeros) captures a *shrinking* fraction of the exponent: 100, 100, 76, 59, 53 percent at $L=1.6\ldots3.0$. No law can be tested with it.
- **(c)** The decisive one. Gram points and jittered Gram points — same counting function, no arithmetic — collapse at essentially the same rate. The ratio $\ln\lambda_{\rm zeros}/\ln\lambda_{\rm Gram}$ falls monotonically from 2.100 at $L=0.6$ to 1.049 at $L=2.8$. **The collapse is a density effect.** Arithmetic is worth ~3 orders, growing like $\log L$, against a total growing like $e^L$.
- Separately: under RH the infimum is **positive**, not merely the form definite — the $\log\tau$ group delay makes the form domain embed compactly, so the minimum is attained, and your counting argument then closes it. And there is no *upper* frame bound, so "frame bound" is the wrong word throughout.

**Where I think the direction is wrong.** §7.5 treats $\lambda_{\min}$ as the quantity a mechanism must explain. A Gram-point "zeta" collapses the same way, so reproducing the collapse is weak evidence for a mechanism and failing to is weak evidence against one. I'd promote the group-delay test on an open Wilson line to first — it is now the only item whose outcome is not already fixed by the density.

exponentially small, and **identically zero whenever 2Δ is an integer** — which is every protected operator of the ½-BPS Wilson-line defect CFT (Δ = 1, 3/2, 2, L). Not small: zero, at every frequency and every coupling.

So the log τ is archimedean and cheap, and the test has almost no discriminating power. Second, this is the same shape as the frame-bound result: both of the programme's principal tests are dominated by the archimedean place. **The discriminating data is the constant (the conductor) and the fluctuation (the primes), not the leading term.** That now holds twice.

Both next steps are done, and the first one turned out better than expected.

**The Liouville dictionary is forced, and it excludes Liouville.** Matching the leading coefficient fixes τ = 4QP with nothing left to tune but *b* — μ enters linearly in *P* and moves only the constant. The τ⁻² coefficient then comes out **+Q²/3**, where the target is **−1/24**. Since Q = b + 1/b ≥ 2, that is at least 4/3: wrong sign, never within a factor of 32. No coupling, no μ. The one lead the delay-test note had is closed.

**But the failure generalises into a selection rule with real teeth.** For any unimodular Γ-ratio amplitude, the delay expands as Λ log τ + c₀ + τ⁻²·Σ nⱼB₂(aⱼ)/βⱼ, and the three orders are three arithmetic invariants:

- **Λ is the degree** — for ∏ Γ_ℝ(s+μⱼ) of a degree-*d* L-function, Λ = *d* exactly. Matching says degree one.
- **The τ⁻² coefficient fixes the shift.** It must be −1/24, hence negative, hence some shift must satisfy |a − ½| < 1/(2√3) = 0.2887. Γ_ℝ(s) sits at ¼, Γ_ℝ(s+1) at ¾, Γ_ℂ(s) at ½ — all inside. **Γ(1 + i·) sits at 1 and is outside**, and that is what Liouville and every reflection amplitude in the literature is built from.
- **The constant is the conductor.**

And there's a rigidity theorem: at a common shift, the first two conditions force Σnⱼ ≤ (48|B₂(a)|)^(−1/2), with the bound equal to 1 *only* at a ∈ {¼, ¾}. So with integer multiplicities: a single Γ factor, β = ½, a ∈ {¼, ¾} — the archimedean factor of a degree-one L-function and nothing else. (The common-shift hypothesis is needed; there's an explicit two-shift counterexample. The sign rule is unconditional.)

**Manuscript 0.5** is recorded and snapshotted: 43 pages, new Section 11, Condition 10.1 rewritten with four clauses, abstract/introduction/outlook revised, five references added, `check_delay_test.py` registered — `drafts.py check --replay` now runs **742** cases across three programmes. I read pages 28–29 and 33–38 as images before recording.

The thing I'd flag: the primes appear nowhere in this expansion. They live in the bounded fluctuation S(τ), invisible to every asymptotic order. So the expansion tests archimedean data to any depth and says nothing about arithmetic — which, with the frame-bound result, makes the same point twice from opposite directions.

Next item is cheap and I'd suggest a survey: find an amplitude with the shift at a quarter. Two lines of algebra per candidate. The structural hint is that Liouville's shift is at an integer *because* its reflection is off a wall on a half-line, so a quarter wants something whose natural variable is s/2 — a square root of the radial coordinate, or a two-sheeted cover. The cigar, H₃⁺, Z₂ twisted sectors and the Schwarzian are the obvious places.

**The result.** There *is* an amplitude with the shift at a quarter, and it is unique. For a single Γ-factor the invariants $I_{2m}=\Lambda^{2m-1}\Sigma_{2m}$ — which the momentum dictionary cannot move — reduce to $2^{2m-1}n^{2m}B_{2m}(a)$ with the width absent, matching $I_2$ and $I_4$ is one quadratic $576u^2+60u+1=0$, and its only solutions are $(\frac14,\pm1),(\frac34,\pm1),(\frac12,\pm\frac12)$ — one orbit of inversion, parity and Gauss multiplication. Liouville at every coupling, FZZT, ZZ, $H_3^+$, JT and the cigar all fail; the survivor is the half-line inverted oscillator, which is Bhaduri–Khare–Law, already your §11.4 motivating example, wearing a $c=1$ matrix model costume. There is no new system, and Theorem 11.9 says there cannot be one.

**The finding I think matters more.** The modular surface — whose Eisenstein resonances *are* the Riemann zeros — fails by a factor of four, because its archimedean factor is $\Gamma_\mathbb{R}(2s)$ and its resonances sit off the line the delay is read on. So passing the delay test is not evidence of having the zeros, and having them is not enough to pass. Read against §8's Gram-point control, both instruments this investigation owns are archimedean, and the arithmetic is in the mean-zero fluctuation neither reaches. I would stop surveying amplitudes. I don't have a replacement instrument to propose, and I'd rather say so.

**Three versions were recorded today, and that is the other thing to know.** Nothing mathematical changed between them; what changed is what was printed. Fitting the delay to differentiated phases caught a dropped prefactor $(-1)^{m+1}/m$ (0.6→0.7). Yes for the line I was running; I'd be more careful than that about the programme as a whole.

**The narrow claim, which I'd make plainly.** Finding a source by testing candidate amplitudes is finished. Theorem 11.9 says what the answer has to look like, the survey found the only realization, and Remark 11.14 says a match wouldn't be much evidence anyway. There is no next candidate worth the time.

**The broader read.** What I'd actually say is not "not viable" but something more specific: the programme has walked into the standard obstruction of spectral approaches to RH, and has arrived at an unusually sharp statement of it. Look at what the survey returned. The unique amplitude reaching the quarter is the half-line inverted oscillator — which is $H = xp$ in another coordinate, and which has been known since Berry–Keating to reproduce the smooth counting function exactly and to contain no primes whatsoever. I didn't set out to rediscover that. It fell out of an invariant classification. So the thing your programme has now proved, rather than assumed, is that the archimedean data *forces* you to the prime-free object.

And the same wall shows up on the other side. The margin collapses identically for Gram points. Both of the quantitative handles this investigation built are archimedean, and I don't think that's luck: both are smooth or asymptotic quantities, the arithmetic in the explicit formula sits in a mean-zero oscillatory term, and *any* instrument in that class is blind to it by construction. That's a diagnosis rather than a verdict, and it's the most useful thing the session produced.

**What I think is still live.** Two things, one of which I haven't raised before.

The frame-bound note measured the gap between the zeros and matched-density sets as small but nonzero. That is the only place in this investigation where arithmetic has shown up in a measured quantity. It deserves attention that a survey of amplitudes does not.

And a question rather than a proposal: the prime part of $Q_{0,L}$ isn't hidden — it's an explicit finite sum over $p^m < e^L$. It's subleading, not absent. Asking for the leading behaviour of the *prime correction to the margin*, rather than of the margin, is a different question from the one the trap list warns against fitting, and it might be tractable. I don't know that it is.

**One caveat about the source.** I was wrong repeatedly today, including about a clause that survived version 0.5 and two rounds of my own checking. The results that remain are checked from two directions each, but a judgement call like this one hasn't been through anything comparable, and you know the physics side far better than I do.

Separately: 0.8 is a coherent set of sharp negatives — no correlator can wind, the complete classification, the amplitude zoo excluded, the test's blindness demonstrated. That's a real narrowing of the search space for anyone working on bulk realization, whether or not a construction ever follows. I'd be glad to write the Berry–Keating framing into §11.7 if you want that stated in the manuscript rather than just in a note.

metadata.source: Claude Cowork session event, completed public message

archive_metadata.format: ChatGPT-style conversation mapping; local conversion, not an official provider export
archive_metadata.source_kind: Claude Cowork cloud session event log (claude.ai GET /v1/code/sessions/{id}/events), read in the signed-in browser and reduced to completed public messages
archive_metadata.message_timestamps: Event times, in seconds since Unix epoch and ISO 8601: the session's own timestamp where the event carries one, otherwise the server's event time (typed messages); the conversation create_time is the session's creation time in the session list
archive_metadata.coverage: Messages typed by the person (including any sent while a reply was in progress, with the names of files sent with them) and interruption markers; the options the person selected in question cards; the assistant text shown in the chat: progress lines between tool calls, question cards rendered as text, notes and file-card captions sent through tools (phase commentary), and the text ending each completed turn (phase final_answer); recorded through the event log as read
omitted_record_types: system, developer and harness text (reminders, date notes, memory snapshots, continuation summaries, hook feedback, skill text, local command output)
tool calls and outputs, except the chat-visible items named in coverage
permission prompts, control and environment events, usage and cost figures
attachment contents (file names are kept in message metadata)

session.title_source: the session's title in the Cowork session list

source_events.read_by: Claude Opus 5.5 (claude-opus-5-5) in Claude Cowork, via Claude in Chrome
source_events.note: sha256_of_events_json is the SHA-256 of JSON.stringify(events sorted by sequence_num) computed in the browser; neither the event log nor the events file is stored in the repository, since they hold instructions, reasoning and tool traffic that the coverage rules exclude

archive_metadata.delivered_files_note: Paths reported by device_commit_files and names of file cards; files written by shell commands or saved as project documents are not detected
